definition: Fetching the k best-scoring chunks for a query.
details: Fetching the k best-scoring chunks for a query. k balances recall against context budget and distraction; typical systems retrieve wide (20-100) then rerank down to a few.

explainer.lead: Top-k retrieval fetches the k best-scoring chunks for a query. It matters because k sets the balance between recall, context budget and distraction from irrelevant text.

tiers.eli5: You pull the k most relevant pages from a library shelf before answering. Too few and you miss the answer; too many and the clutter buries it.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers typically retrieve wide, 20-100 chunks, then rerank down to a few. A pitfall is passing the whole wide set to the model, wasting context and distracting it.
tiers.paperLevel: Select the k highest-scoring chunks under a retrieval score. Limits: recall depends on k, while context budget and distraction grow with it.

explainer.example: A system fetches the top 50 chunks by similarity, reranks them, and passes only the best 3 to the model.
